payload.author: lzjackm
payload.body:
## TL;DR

The `hyperliquid-hlp` adapter's allocation prediction over-states actual on-chain HLP accrual by an amount that scales with HIP-3 fee share. The mechanism appears to be that HIP-3 Growth Mode markets (90% reduced taker fees per the documented launch on 2025-11-19) generate ~10× less in actually-collected protocol fees per unit of underlying volume, but the revenue base used by the `hyperliquid-hlp` adapter still tracks fees at a higher basis.

Empirically: the relationship `ratio = 0.97 − 1.11 × HIP-3_fee_share` (R² = 0.78) describes the post-Aug-30 trajectory cleanly. The Hypurrscan-based prediction (used by the same adapter pre-2025-08-01) tracks closer to observed but still has the same HIP-3-share-dependent decline at smaller magnitude.

## Empirical evidence

| Period | DL-indexer prediction | Hypurrscan-based prediction | Observed HLP accrual | Obs / DL | Obs / Hyp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-rate (Mar 26 – Aug 29 2025) | $12.05M | $11.64M | $11.49M | 95.4% | 98.7% |
| Post-rate (Aug 30 2025 – May 18 2026) | $6.40M | $5.33M | $5.22M | 81.6% | 97.9% |
| Full window | $18.45M | $16.97M | $16.71M | 90.6% | 98.5% |

**Observed HLP accrual** = parent HLP vault's `pnl_since_inception` delta on `0xdfc24b077bc1425ad1dea75bcb6f8158e10df303`, scope=perp, from HL's `vaultDetails` API (allTime timeframe). The parent vault has zero direct fills, zero positions, zero funding — its PnL accrual is exclusively system-level fee credits. Cross-verified by the identity `parent scope=all = parent scope=perp + Σ(children scope=perp)`, within $18K on a $76M window.

**Predictions** apply `hlpShare × (perp_fees + spot_fees)` with `hlpShare = 0.03` pre-2025-08-30, `0.01` post, per `getRevenueRatioShares` in `helpers/hyperliquid.ts`.

## Mechanism: HIP-3 share drives the divergence

Linear regression on monthly Hypurrscan-based ratios for the post-Aug-30 period (n=7, excluding Sep 2025 rate-transition month as outlier):

```
ratio = 0.97 − 1.11 × HIP-3_fee_share         (R² = 0.78)

Time index does NOT add information beyond HIP-3 share (p = 0.95).
HIP-3 share alone is a sufficient explanatory variable.
```

Per-month predicted vs observed:

```
Month     HIP-3 share   Predicted   Observed   Residual
2025-10      0.0%         97.0%       94.8%     −2.2%
2025-11      2.3%         94.5%       94.0%     −0.5%
2025-12      2.2%         94.6%       96.2%     +1.6%
2026-01      7.2%         89.1%       94.8%     +5.7%
2026-02      8.3%         87.9%       84.5%     −3.4%
2026-03     13.1%         82.5%       81.4%     −1.1%
2026-04     12.1%         83.7%       83.6%     −0.1%
```

Coefficient interpretation: each 1pp of HIP-3 fee share lowers the observed-vs-predicted ratio by 1.11pp. This is approximately consistent with **HIP-3 markets contributing zero to HLP allocation per unit of fee in the reference base** — because Growth Mode (launched Nov 19 2025) reduces protocol fees by 90% on activated markets, and HLP receives 1% of *actually-collected* fees. If the reference base tracks fees at full-rate basis (or user-paid amount before Growth Mode reduction), each 1pp of HIP-3 share in the reference shows up as ~1pp of "missing" HLP allocation.

The HIP-3 spec ([docs](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hyperliquid-improvement-proposals-hips/hip-3-builder-deployed-perpetuals)) confirms that HIP-3 deployers can keep up to 50% of fees as markup, but the **Growth Mode-specific 90% fee cut** is the dominant effect — HIP-3 share at 12% (April 2026) shifts the predicted ratio by ~13pp vs the ~6pp that deployer markup alone (50% of HIP-3 fees) would predict.

## Reproduction

```python
import requests, pandas as pd

# Hypurrscan-based HLP allocation prediction (Mar 26 2025 → May 18 2026)
d = requests.get('https://api.hypurrscan.io/fees').json()
df = pd.DataFrame(d)
df['ts'] = pd.to_datetime(df['time'], unit='s')
df['total_fees_usd'] = df['total_fees'] / 1e6  # matches adapter's /1e6

def at(target):
    return df.iloc[(df['ts'] - t
payload.title: [hyperliquid-hlp] HLP allocation prediction diverges with HIP-3 share growth (~3-17%); HIP-3 Growth Mode fee reduction not reflected in revenue base

payload.author: tarun-khatri
payload.body:
The Convex fees adapter at \`fees/convex.ts\` has been silently broken since 2026-05-06. Filing for visibility (cc @benber86 since you maintain this file).

## Evidence

**1. Adapter source still points at a now-deindexed subgraph**

[`fees/convex.ts:11`](https://github.com/DefiLlama/dimension-adapters/blob/master/fees/convex.ts#L11) calls:

\`\`\`ts
sdk.graph.modifyEndpoint('86irRVuFotfaCFwtFxiSaJ76Y8pxfU3xX91gU6CoYTvi')
\`\`\`

That subgraph ID is no longer indexed. The Graph's public hosted-service endpoint replies definitively:

\`\`\`
$ curl -s -X POST https://api.thegraph.com/subgraphs/id/86irRVuFotfaCFwtFxiSaJ76Y8pxfU3xX91gU6CoYTvi -d '{"query":"{_meta{block{number}}}"}'
{"errors":[{"message":"deployment \`86irRVuFotfaCFwtFxiSaJ76Y8pxfU3xX91gU6CoYTvi\` does not exist"}]}
\`\`\`

The gateway endpoint with auth returns the rate-limit error, but the hosted-service \`does not exist\` reply confirms this isn't a quota issue — the deployment itself is gone.

**2. DefiLlama's fees chart for Convex shows the break date precisely**

\`api.llama.fi/summary/fees/convex-finance\` returns 1815 daily data points through **2026-05-06** ($23k–$60k/day range) and then **no entries** for 2026-05-07 through today (8+ days of missing data).

Sample tail:

| date | dailyFees (USD) |
|------|---:|
| 2026-05-06 | 49,697 |
| 2026-05-05 | 57,337 |
| 2026-05-04 | 23,033 |
| 2026-05-03 | 51,930 |
| 2026-05-02 | 57,533 |
| *2026-05-07 onward* | *(no data)* |

The current values are:
\`\`\`
total24h: null
total7d:  null
total30d: 1,028,508
totalAllTime: 1,726,948,487
\`\`\`

**3. Convex itself is very much alive** — \`api.llama.fi/protocol/convex-finance\` reports \$611M TVL on Ethereum, \$7.6M on Fraxtal, \$2.4M on Arbitrum.

So the bug is adapter-side, not protocol-side. ~$1M/30d of fees are silently going untracked on a top-50 TVL protocol.

## Suggested fixes

Three rough paths (in order of effort):

1. **Replace the subgraph hash** with the current Convex revenue subgraph. \`Llama-Airforce-Net\` reads from a \`GRAPH_CONVEX\` env var that presumably points at the new deployment — if @benber86 can share the public ID, swapping line 11 is a one-line fix.

2. **Switch to an alternative data source.** \`api.llama.airforce/dashboard/bribes-overview-votium\` (used in this same adapter for the Votium bribes path) works fine, but doesn't carry the full \`dailyRevenueSnapshot\` payload.

3. **On-chain rewrite** — track CRV / CVX / FXS distributions via Transfer events from the relevant Booster/Reward contracts. Significantly more code (~200 lines).

Happy to PR any of these if there's a preferred direction.

Two issues with the Pendle fees adapter:

**1. Protocol revenue reported before September 2025**

The adapter is currently returning protocol revenue for dates prior to September 2025. According to the Pendle team, there was no protocol-level revenue before that date, these values should be zero. The current data shows protocol revenue going back to December 2023, totalling ~$8.3M in incorrectly attributed protocol revenue across 21 months.

**Expected behaviour:** `protocolRevenue` should return `0` / `null` for all dates before September 2025.

**2. Double counting in revenue figures**

There also appears to be double counting in the overall revenue numbers. Revenue components (holders revenue, protocol revenue, supply side revenue) don't consistently sum to the reported total, in Pendles team Dune suggesting certain fee flows are being counted more than once.

**Reference sources from the Pendle team:**
- Dune dashboard with full revenue calculation methodology: https://dune.com/p_team/pendle-tvl-and-revenue
- V2 revenue calculation instructions for third-party data platforms: https://pendle.notion.site/3rd-party-Data-Platform-Pendle-V2-Revenue-Calculation-Instruction-224567a21d3780afac7ef668866b4d71

**Adapter file:** https://github.com/DefiLlama/dimension-adapters/blob/master/fees/pendle.ts

payload.author: KlementMultiverse
payload.body:
## Problem

The dimension-adapters repo has 60+ open fee-tracking issues for individual protocols (Marginfi, 0xfreelance, Axe Cap, Brewlabs, etc.), but many of these are duplicates of the same underlying work: extracting daily gas fees from EVM chains. Each protocol submitter writes similar boilerplate to query gas metrics, normalize data, and handle chain-specific RPC quirks.

Related: #5827 "Add generic evm fees/txns/gas used adapter" attempts this but lacks a reusable template and integration docs.

## Why This Matters

1. **Unblocks 40+ pending issues** — Protocol teams can use a template instead of waiting for maintainers to build individual adapters
2. **Reduces maintenance burden** — One shared implementation for gas tracking beats maintaining 60 similar adapters
3. **Lowers contribution friction** — New protocol submissions become a 10-minute config task, not a 2-hour coding task

## What Good Looks Like

Create a template adapter at `adapters/fees/evm-generic-gas/template.ts` that:

1. **Provides a configurable factory function** that accepts:
   - Chain name (ethereum, arbitrum, polygon, etc.)
   - Block range (for backfill)
   - Optional gas price multiplier (for protocol-specific adjustments)

2. **Implements standard gas fee logic** once:
   - Query block timestamps and base fees via RPC `eth_getBlockByNumber`
   - Calculate daily aggregates (sum of block base fees)
   - Handle chain-specific gas mechanisms (EIP-1559, priority fees)
   - Normalize to USD using a configurable price oracle

3. **Includes documented examples** for:
   - Simple case: "My protocol charges users 0.5% of gas fees" → 2-line config
   - Complex case: "My protocol only charges on certain transaction types" → override handler

4. **Exports a `createGasFeesAdapter()` helper** so submissions look like:
   ```typescript
   export default createGasFeesAdapter({
     chain: 'arbitrum',
     startBlock: 15000000,
     priceMultiplier: 0.005
   })
   ```

## Acceptance Criteria

- Template handles Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, Optimism, BSC
- Includes 3 end-to-end example implementations (picking 3 from pending issues)
- Passes `pnpm test fees <chain>` without errors
- Reduces per-protocol adapter code from ~150 lines to ~20 lines
- Documents the pattern in README with a link from docs/list-your-project

## Files to Update

- Create `adapters/fees/evm-generic-gas/template.ts` + `index.ts`
- Update `README.md` with template usage instructions
- Convert 3 pending protocol issues to use the template as proof


---
*Contributed by [Klement Gunndu](https://github.com/KlementMultiverse)*
payload.title: Create reusable EVM gas fees adapter template to reduce protocol-specific duplication

payload.author: dashboardsdata
payload.body:
https://x.com/o1_exchange is not the same as 01 exchange which is what is shown on the front end (https://defillama.com/protocol/01).

@noateden has pr'ed removing the base fees (which is where o1_exchange dominates) and there is confusion regarding which protocol this data is regarding (see the title of this commit https://github.com/DefiLlama/dimension-adapters/commit/1f1276035378f7c3276e6494f08a76fc45693762).

I worked with the team to do the work on dune so my commit (https://github.com/DefiLlama/dimension-adapters/commit/1f1276035378f7c3276e6494f08a76fc45693762) should be accurate although it may not be the most efficient.

If we could get these fixed it would be great, thank you!
payload.title: o1 exchange data is being attributed to incorrect protocol called 01

payload.author: treeoflife2
payload.body:
https://defillama.com/protocol/yield-basis

1. distributor for VeYB: 0xD11b416573EbC59b6B2387DA0D2c0D1b3b1F7A90
2. plain LT holders (unstaked market deposits) earnings: LT.pricePerShare growth essentially. tvl*(ppsNow - ppsPast)/(ppsPast). ppsPast can be 1h ago.

so part of the fees come as admin fees and get collected into distributor for veyb
the other part goes into market/LT pricePerShare, easiest to calculate is how i mentioned at 2.
